title: Faith, repentance, and renovating grace not denied
source_text: XX. Caeterum minime per id negare volunt fidei verae vivaeque, & seriae ac syncerae poenitentiae actus in nobis a Deo requiri, ut propter Christi mortem & obedientiam, remissionis peccatorum nostrorum, & adoptionis in Dei Filios participes fiamus. Ac praeterea Christum morte & passione sua non solum fideles reatu peccatorum solvere, sed eam quoque ipsis gratiam promeruisse, per quam ad Dei Christique imaginem renoventur, veraque justitia & sanctitate induantur. Quae justitia, licet his in terris ad summum perfectionis gradum non proveniat, & multis ex infirmitate lapsibus obscuretur, non deficit tamen in essentialibus, Deoque grata atque accepta est: ac quamvis per eam fideles non possint coram Deo justificari, si Deus erga ipsos nulla indulgentia & clementia uti velit, nihilominus promissionem habet vitae & gloriae aeternae; quam Deus illi olim ultimo die, juxta Evangelium gratiae mundum judicans, misericorditer & fideliter reddet.
pass_a_gloss: Yet by this they by no means wish to deny that acts of true and living faith and of serious and sincere repentance are required in us by God so that for the sake of Christ’s death and obedience we become partakers of the remission of our sins and of adoption as God’s children. And further, that by his death and passion Christ not only frees the faithful from the guilt of sins, but also merited for them that grace by which they are renewed to the image of God and Christ and are clothed with true righteousness and holiness. Which righteousness, though on earth it does not reach the highest degree of perfection and is obscured by many lapses from infirmity, yet does not fail in essentials and is pleasing and acceptable to God; and although by it the faithful cannot be justified before God if God wills to use no indulgence and clemency toward them, nevertheless it has the promise of eternal life and glory, which God will one day mercifully and faithfully render to it on the last day when judging the world according to the gospel of grace.
pass_b_english: Imputation does not cancel required living faith and sincere repentance.
Christ also merited renovating grace; inherent holiness, though imperfect, is accepted and promised glory.
